name: shunt
summary: An S3 proxy that moves a live bucket from one cluster to another while clients keep reading and writing it. Same endpoint, same bucket name, same keys. When the move is done, it steps out of the way.
note: Proof of concept. It has run on Garage, MinIO and VAST.

name: mongoose
summary: Copies everything under one NFS path to another, keeps the copy current while people still use the old server, and cuts over only when every file reads back identical from both.
note: One static binary. It speaks NFSv3 itself, so nothing gets mounted.

name: vamoose
summary: The distributed edition of mongoose. Workers on many hosts copy NFS to NFS from a Parquet index and claim shards with conditional writes in S3, so no central service decides who copies what.
note: An optional coordinator and terminal dashboard add stop, resume and abort.

name: nfs-walker
summary: Walks an NFS export with READDIRPLUS and work-stealing threads, and streams every entry into sharded Parquet. The same binary serves a web dashboard that runs 36 queries over the scan.
note: 810 million files in under 20 minutes, from one host.

name: nfs-gaze
summary: Watches NFS client latency one operation at a time, READ, WRITE, GETATTR and the rest, straight from /proc/self/mountstats. No kernel module, no eBPF.
note: Filter to the ops you care about, snapshot to JSON, export to Prometheus.

name: s3slower
summary: Times every S3 request leaving a Linux host from inside the TLS libraries, with eBPF. It works with any client and needs no SDK wrapper, no proxy and no code change.
note: Prometheus metrics on port 9000, installed as one RPM.

name: s3lister
summary: Similar to nfs-walker, but for s3.  Lists all the objects in a bucket, very quickly with many thread and creates a parquetdb to help with analysis of the data.
note: 227 million objects nested deap in 7 minutes.

name: vast-bucket-policy-manager
summary: A terminal UI for listing, editing and applying S3 bucket policies on VAST, AWS or any S3 store. It checks the JSON and the IAM structure as you type.
note: Every save and delete writes a before-and-after backup first.
